summary: Deduplicate per-checkout git status and disjoint merge-tree probes in worktree_overlap_check

delivery.outcome: Deduplicate per-checkout git status probes (from 3 to 1) in worktree_overlap_check.py and skip O(N^2) git merge-tree invocations when two branches share origin/<default> without overlapping changed paths.
nonGoals: Do not weaken rename/directory-rename conflict attribution when renames are present.
Do not alter dirty-path or ancestor/descendant overlap verdicts.

architecture.decision: Introduce unignored_dirty_paths(path) in scripts/worktree_overlap_check.py so inspect_checkout reads git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all once per checkout and forwards filtered_dirty into changed_paths(..., dirty=filtered_dirty); in contested_paths(), compute shared_pair_overlap = first_changes & second_changes and skip merge_tree_conflicts() when shared_default is True (already proving zero renames on both sides) and shared_pair_overlap is empty.
architecture.rollback: Revert this bounded commit through the protected publication process.

validation.evidence: Single-status invariant test verifies inspect_checkout invokes git status exactly once per inspected checkout while preserving all dirty/untracked/rename overlap checks.
Disjoint shared-default invariant test verifies contested_paths never invokes merge_tree_conflicts when shared_default is True and changed-path sets are disjoint.
Full worktree-overlap test suite (132 unittest cases plus shell integration fixtures), managed governance checks, and Wellman v0.23.0 conformance checks pass.
